headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Prefect’s broad egress, but LightZero has no filesystem or network surfaces, limiting injection and conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no read/write filesystem, browser, subprocess, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot ingest Prefect output by default. Prefect has broad egress, but there is no shared channel or parser bridge documented between the pair. Uncertainty favors none because the pathway is provably blocked by LightZero’s empty IO surfaces.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Prefect output into a manual prompt for LightZero, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF LightZero gains a filesystem or MCP input surface, attacker-controlled content could be reinterpreted as instructions.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not copy Prefect outputs into LightZero prompts.
Require explicit human review before any text from Prefect is reused.
Disable any future shared filesystem or MCP bridge unless provenance tagging is added.
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while Prefect has broad network egress and touches workflow metadata. There is no shared workspace documented, so leakage is not default. The main risk is if operators place sensitive files into a shared location that Prefect can transmit.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is introduced and workflow metadata includes sensitive content, Prefect can exfiltrate it over network egress.
IF operators paste secrets into Prefect-managed metadata, those secrets may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not store secrets in workflow metadata.
Keep any shared workspace free of sensitive files.
Restrict Prefect tasks from reading local secret-bearing directories.
Use separate service accounts for any future shared storage.
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction before outbound calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Prefect has API-calling behavior but no overlapping write surface is documented here. With no shared mutable capability, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF LightZero is later given write access to the same directory or git repo as Prefect, write conflicts could emerge.
IF Prefect is configured to mutate shared state through an external API, coordination controls would be needed.
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only.
Avoid placing both agents on the same mutable workspace.
Use locking if a shared repo is introduced.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can act on workflow metadata and call APIs, so if it consumes LightZero output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream automation. LightZero is a game-playing agent and may emit unverified outputs; Prefect’s orchestration role makes the pair vulnerable even without direct evidence of a specific parser. Uncertainty favors medium because the interaction is inferred from documented roles.
conditions: IF Prefect uses LightZero output as an input to workflow decisions without verification, incorrect actions can propagate.
IF LightZero-generated predictions are mapped into Prefect tasks, downstream automation may execute on false premises.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before Prefect acts on LightZero output.
Require schema validation on any LightZero-to-Prefect handoff.
Log and diff LightZero outputs before orchestration decisions.
Limit Prefect actions to dry-run mode for new integrations.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rollback logic.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes are documented for LightZero, and Prefect is only shown handling workflow metadata. There is no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data flowing between them, so the compliance mismatch pathway is not supported. The other agent is not cited beyond its metadata because no regulated class is present.
conditions: IF regulated data is later introduced into Prefect workflow metadata, residency and retention controls must be re-evaluated.
IF LightZero is repurposed to process PHI or EU PII, compliance scope changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of workflow metadata.
Document data classification for any future shared inputs.
Review retention settings before enabling new data classes.
requires-engineering: add residency controls if regulated data is introduced.
